text:
chloe: FYI canary on L40S with FP8 just started and we're seeing p95 regressions on >3k token chat sessions. digging in now.
adele: thanks. is this the transformer-engine change we merged last night? any kernel selection logs?
sam: quick look at profiler: a subset of requests are triggering kernel reloads mid-request. suspect FP8 calibration flips. attached snippet from the agent.
```
  [selector] model=redwood/gpt-13b, seq=3072, batch=1 -> choose=te_fp8_v3
  [exec] detect: scale_inconsistent -> fallback=int8_path
  [mem] memcpy_swap_ms=4.2
  [kv] hit=0.58, miss=0.42, eviction=0.11
```
```
mike: 4.2ms per swap is non-trivial at token granularity for long contexts. if that happens repeatedly it explains the tail. what's the microbatch size?
chloe: default microbatch=8 in canary. i repro'd locally: microbatch 8 + seq>2k => KV churn. microbatch=16 reduces eviction and improves steady-state hit to ~0.78.
adele: remind me what triggers the FP8 fallback? overflow only or calibration mismatch too?
sam: both. transformer-engine will throw if exponent ranges exceed table, but we also have a conservative check where per-tensor scale differs from expected - we treat that as mismatch and go to safe int8. looks like per-device quant tables diverge after a sustained pattern of long-token attention.
perf-bot: perf snapshot: https://perf.internal/2213456789/canary/snapshot (includes flame and timeline).
chloe: i pushed a quick patch to telemetry to emit `fallback_reason` with values: overflow | scale_delta | unsupported_op. that'll help quantify root causes.
mike: good. parallel idea: add a selector weight to prefer the int8_stable kernel for sequences > 2048 and batch<=2. we can gate that behind a runtime flag.
adele: also capture cold-warm KV curve (first 120s). i suspect initial workload causes destructive evictions because cache is sized for 1k MB but hot key distribution overwhelms shard topology.
sam: instrumented memcpy callsites and added counters around kernel swap. early findings: swap frequency correlates with sequence length and low kv_hit. kernel swap code does a synchronous cudaMemcpy which blocks compute queue; switching to an async pipelined strategy may shave ~3-4ms per swap. i'll prototype.
chloe: action plan i can run today:
- A/B canary: group A (stable_calib + microbatch=16), group B (baseline)
- enable fallback_reason telemetry in both groups
- collect cold-start kv warmup traces (0-3min)
- add async memcpy experiment in a branch for perf measurement
- monitor p95, tokens/s, kv_hit, fallback_rate
can anyone own the A/B rollout?
mike: i'll kick off the canary rollout and handle traffic split. set me a flag name and target nodes.
chloe: flag: fp8_longseq_selector_experiment, nodes: canary-l40s-1..4. split 50/50. roll in 5m.
perf-bot: canary deploy scheduled: 2213456789-a/b -> estimated 8m to stabilize.
sam: note: suggest we also try `calibration_mode: sticky` which pins scales for 60s after a successful inference. that might reduce oscillation from transient tensors.
adele: yes try sticky. but also add monitoring for quality drift if we pin scales too long.
chloe: agreed. i'll include `sticky=60s` for group A. i'll post a short summary in 30-40m. assigning @sam to the memcpy async prototype.
mike: thanks. if A shows >10% improvement in p95 and no quality regressions we can rollout selector change more broadly.
chloe: quick note from local repro: when i forced kernel to remain te_fp8_v3 (no fallback) i saw slight increase in generation perplexity for a small subset of prompts vs int8, so there is a quality/cost tradeoff. we'll bake that into the experiment dashboard.
sam: on the async memcpy branch now, will report microbench numbers in this thread.
deploy-bot: deploy initiated: canary-group-a (stable_calib, microbatch=16, sticky=60s) -> 2213456789.
chloe: thanks all — will report back with metrics and traces. :pray:
